title: Classical integral stable homotopy groups of spheres, stems 0 through 90
definition: pi_k^S = colim_n pi_{n+k}(S^n), using the homotopy-group grading convention.

representation.primary_decomposition: A map from a prime p to the sorted cyclic orders of the p-primary summands. Example: {"2":[2,8],"3":[3]} means C2 direct-sum C8 direct-sum C3.
representation.integral_decomposition: Z^free_rank direct-sum C_d1 direct-sum ... direct-sum C_dr, where torsion_invariant_factors=[d1,...,dr] and d_i divides d_(i+1).
representation.torsion_order: A decimal string, avoiding JSON integer-width ambiguity. It is the order of the torsion subgroup; it is 1 for a torsion-free or trivial group.
representation.empty_group: free_rank 0 with no primary summands and no torsion invariant factors is the trivial group.

sources.citation: Daniel C. Isaksen, Guozhen Wang, and Zhouli Xu, Stable homotopy groups of spheres: from dimension 0 to 90, Publications mathematiques de l'IHES 137 (2023), 107-243.

sources.registry_use: Table 1 is the base registry. Its notation n^j means j copies of C_n. It explicitly lists alternatives beginning in stem 84.

sources.citation: Robert Burklund, Daniel C. Isaksen, and Zhouli Xu, Classical Stable Homotopy Groups of Spheres via F_2-Synthetic Methods, Peking Mathematical Journal (2025).
sources.registry_use: Section 1.2 corrects the 2-primary v1-torsion in stems 70 and 71. Theorem 1.1 completes the 2-primary components in stems 82 and 83.

caveats: This registry records abstract additive groups, not named generators, products, Toda brackets, Adams filtrations, or spectral-sequence representatives.
Rows 84, 85, 86, and 90 are not exact. Each alternative is a complete integral group, including all known odd-primary and v1-periodic summands.
Do not reconstruct rows 70, 71, 82, or 83 from IWX 2023 alone; the 2025 source corrects or completes them.
Primary decompositions are canonical for finite abelian groups. Integral invariant factors are derived mechanically from them and are included for comparator-friendly equality.
